rows.step: How much of the loop a project starts with, and in what order it grows
rows.pb: Adopt the plays in the order the dependency graph gives, which is not the stage order: start with any clay play (nothing points into it), and adopt any other play only after the plays whose arrows point into it. At first every step is prompted by hand; the end state is a loop in which each accepted artifact fires the next gate. For the design pass the ladder is by hand, then an organization slash command, then a job that fires on the merge. In Build, auto-accept becomes the default for routine work only as the guardrails from the later plays mature. The steps are modular, and organizations may choose to transform different stages at different times, based on their needs.
rows.fw: /sdlc:sdlc-init installs the whole loop in one change-0000 PR: every phase command, hook and gate, the twelve sdlc-*.yml workflows and phase (f)'s detection and scans. The loop runs in CI once the owner adds the Claude secret and lets GitHub Actions open pull requests (sdlc-init §6); until the secret exists every phase run ends green as 'skipped' (the weekly scan fails instead) and each phase is run by hand as a slash command, all phases alike. No setting starts a project with a subset of the plays or adds them in order: the profile sets how many gates wait for the owner, the review mode whether a judgment item parks or goes to the panel, deploy.production only whether a release label is needed, and sdlc.yaml's paused flag stops every phase run at once, not a chosen few. The evals suite starts empty and fills from incidents (D17), and the detection has nothing to watch until the project has CI runs of its own; neither is an adoption step the owner orders. The p.8 order and the p.13 ladder were used to build the framework itself (build guide stages B0 to B5, step 43), not to adopt it in a project.

rows.why: No decision on how a project adopts the framework. Nearest: D1 hosted CI (the p.13 ladder was applied to building the framework: by hand in B1, CI from B3) · D19 phase adapters, so no project skips (e) or (f) · D17 evals start empty
rows.weigh: The article adopts the plays in the p.8 order and runs each step by hand before automating it (p.8, p.13); the framework starts a project at the end state. It has no staged start: the nearest is to hold back the Claude secret, which leaves every phase to be run by hand, all at once. For a new project, is the full loop from the first change what you want, or should the framework offer a staged start?

rows.step: Where intents live and who sets it up
rows.pb: A one-time task for the platform or engineering team: a technical team member stands up the intent home and decides who can write to it. For a single product the simplest home is an intent/ folder in the product repo; a dedicated intent repo is only worth it when intent spans many repositories. The template, which can be encoded as a skill, is set up by a technical team member and signed off by a lead.
rows.fw: /sdlc:sdlc-init writes the project's files into the repository in one change-0000 PR: sdlc.yaml, guardrails, changes/, bands.yaml, evals/, lessons/, workflows. Intents live in changes/<id>-<slug>/ next to the code. Who can write to main is the branch ruleset of D4, which the owner creates by hand after the merge. The intent template is the intent-template skill, which ships in the plugin, so by default a project has no template to set up or sign off.

rows.step: Which human approval gates exist, and where they are enforced
rows.pb: Engineering leadership, with change management and compliance, lists the gates that must survive; the platform engineer expresses each as a hook, with non-negotiable hooks in managed settings.
rows.fw: The gates are fixed by the framework (profiles, labels, confidence gate); per project, sdlc.yaml adds the risk list, protected paths and, on a declared production, the release approval and guarded deploy commands. /sdlc-init asks for the profile, the review mode and whether production is real; the risk list is the template's default, which it does not ask about. Guardrails sit in three layers: the plugin's hooks with project deny rules as a second net; an optional managed settings file, on the owner's machine only, which neither a cloud session nor CI reads; CI loading hooks and permissions from the pinned plugin, never from the PR branch. The owner adds the 'Restrict updates' ruleset.

decision.note: Blend toward the playbook (T18), option C4; C3 if the passing check cannot satisfy the rule, C1's click if the App proves impractical, B's record kept. Gate (e) becomes my approving review on the build PR, informed by the findings, as in the article (amends D13); the agent cannot approve it because it authored it. My approval is my only act: it fires a merge workflow by itself (a review I submit starts workflows); a deterministic step, no model, checks the approval is mine, the PR is a framework build PR at sdlc:e-ready and sdlc/review is green, then merges through a dedicated GitHub App that is a bypass actor of 'Restrict updates' (T1's direction; amends D4 and D5: a second actor may merge, only on my approval). If I approve before the check is green, the (e) run starts the merge workflow when it turns green; a blocked merge shows in the digest; nothing notifies me. Rulesets: today's 'Restrict updates' with my Exempt bypass stays; a second ruleset requires only the sdlc/review check (no required approval, which D4 rejected because my own intent PRs could not pass it), with my bypass in 'pull requests only' mode, and every other PR gets a passing 'not a build PR' sdlc/review on each new head: the steps that open or update an automation PR (design, incident, dismissal, standing; a runbook PR carries T14's own sdlc/review) post it themselves, since the workflow token's PRs and pushes start no workflow run by themselves (their pull_request runs wait for approval), and a small workflow posts it on PRs and pushes made by people; so intent, design, incident and my own PRs merge as today, from the phone too, while an unreviewed build-PR merge needs a deliberate web bypass. The runner posts sdlc/review again on the build PR's final head, after its own last commit (today it re-posts only sdlc/d, and before that commit), and the merge step checks the head it merges against the review findings (no commit after them but evidence), not the check alone. Fallbacks: C3 (no second ruleset; an early merge by hand stays possible and is flagged) if a check posted by the automation cannot satisfy the required check; C1 (I merge after approving) if the App proves impractical. B kept: the runner records the (e) approval and merge (who, when, the findings tally, the banner shown) beside the plan acceptance and the build and test labels. One-time setup per project: the App, its key, the second ruleset (in /sdlc-init §6). To verify: that my approval counts on a PR the automation opened; that a check posted by the automation satisfies the required check, and that a required check binds the head commit; that the web bypass is logged; the App as a bypass actor and its merge workflow, with its key out of reach of workflow files a PR branch can change; whether a push after my approval dismisses it. Considered and not chosen: A (the merge alone) and B alone; C2's ruleset requiring an approval and the check on every PR (it would block intent, design and incident PRs); auto-merge (it merges as whoever enabled it, not verified); an automatic revert PR.

rows.pb: Tier the autonomy by environment: in development the agent deploys freely, staging sits somewhere in the middle, and in production the agent prepares the release and the release manager authorizes it. Deploy, status and rollback become MCP tools scoped per environment, so the agent's deployment powers are an allowlist rather than a shell script with credentials. Rollback is the most rehearsed path in the pipeline: a single command the agent can run, exercised regularly in staging and proven in advance, because the closing-the-loop play calls it when a control band is breached.

Deploy, status and rollback as MCP tools are not built: no MCP server or tool code exists, and build guide step 31 and OPERATING_MODEL §9 defer them (§9: the plugin ships no runtime dependency, and no project has named a real deployment yet). No Claude session deploys, and no agent holds a deploy credential.

A release waiting for its label shows nowhere, since the merged PR is closed and the daily digest lists open PRs only, and nothing in the framework reports a failed release, a red run in Actions. release-notes.md is read by the build PR's body, never by the release workflow.

rows.fw: The one gate function (plugin/gate/gate.py run_gate), in this order: run limits (fix iterations per change, 3 by default and 2 once the adversarial reviewer classes the plan non-routine, never below 1; panel calls under deferred review, 4; 120 minutes per phase run; the optional dollar cap against the change's running total, CI only; the paused flag), then the phase's deterministic checks ((a): artifacts, design scope, guardrails, the risk list; (b): those plus open concerns, the panel, commands and the owner's actions; (c) to (e): artifacts, open concerns, the panel, commands, evidence, findings, plan sync, guardrails, the risk list, the owner's actions, the test lock and a clean tree, no design scope; (f): artifacts, design scope, guardrails, the risk list, the finding and its route), then the adversarial verdict, required at (b), (c) and (d) and judged at (e) when one is there; the REVIEW.md pass's findings file is required at (e), and an open Important finding fails the gate wherever a findings file exists; (a) and (f) are deterministic only. A crashing check parks, never passes; a crash in the run limits themselves ends the gate command with a traceback. The reviewer runs on the session's own model (model: inherit), has no shell, returns continue or escalate with reasons and classes the plan routine or non-routine; the class only lowers the iteration cap. Three results: continue records the gate as passed and the runner dispatches the next workflow (workflow_dispatch, since the workflow token's own events start nothing); wait stops at a human gate with sdlc:<phase>-ready (Standard: a, b, e and f; Full: all); park writes status.yaml parked_reason, evidence/gate-<phase>.json with the failed check and 'What I need from you', and labels the PR sdlc:needs-human; nobody is notified. Under deferred review a fixed list goes to the panel instead of parking (an open flagged concern, contradicting policy skills, an escalate verdict, an Important finding the run cannot fix, a verifier disagreement), while the hard parks stay (a risk-list hit, a guardrail file change, a run limit, an infrastructure failure, anything that merges or deploys). Exit codes: gate/cli.py check 0 continue, 3 wait, 4 park, 2 a usage error; run_phase.py 0 finished, skipped or parked, 1 an infrastructure failure, 2 a usage error. The owner's merges of the intent and design PRs start the design and build workflows (both fire on every merged PR to the default branch and find the change from it, so the merge of an incident intent PR at (f) starts the design run too); the owner's merge at (e) starts the release workflow; the runner's dispatch starts test and deploy under Standard, the owner's approval labels under Full; a 'Request changes' review or an un-park label starts the fix round. rows.step: Sandbox, tokens and identity of agent jobs
rows.pb: Agent jobs run in containers under a network policy with short-lived scoped tokens and no standing production credentials. Each non-interactive run acts under the agent's own identity, so the log separates what the agent did from what the person who triggered it did.
rows.fw: Every phase job runs claude -p on an ephemeral GitHub runner with settings from the pinned framework: the sandbox is mandatory, the network is limited to the API, GitHub and package registries, secrets and web tools are denied and bypass is disabled. The session gets one model credential (the runner drops the other) and commits as github-actions[bot]. No phase job holds a deploy secret; the release job runs deploy.command with no Claude session. The workflow token is in the environment of every phase, fix and detect session (not the weekly scan's review, not the eval runs), with each workflow's permissions (contents, pull requests, issues and checks write; actions write in the phase and fix workflows, read in detect), and, since no workflow sets persist-credentials, in every checkout's .git/config, the scan's and the eval runs' included. The session uses it to fetch, pull and push its branch, to open and update its pull request (the runner repeats the update after the session; only the session marks the (e) pull request ready), to post the gate (d) and sdlc/review check runs, and to read checks (gh pr checks) and failed runs (gh run view); the runner parks a session that pushed to another of the change's sdlc/<id>/* branches than the one it prepared, one that ends on another branch than the one it prepared (0.3.6, PR #130: the checkout is put back first, and the park, the result record and the spend entry are written on the prepared branch), or one whose sdlc/<id>/* branch has a remote tip its checkout does not contain; a push to any other branch is not detected, and the ruleset leaves the token no route to main (D4). The model credential is inherited by every sandboxed command, though none needs it. The CI settings' Edit deny rules on .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md and sdlc.yaml are also the sandbox's write-deny list according to the settings reference, so a shell write to CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md and sdlc.yaml should already fail (not verified on a runner); .claude/** is a glob, which the sandbox skips on Linux by the same documentation, so it may be open; the project's protected_paths and the pinned framework checkout at framework/, which holds the hooks, are not denied. The scan's open finding on this repository (change 0002, PR #118) says a python or node write reaches CLAUDE.md; it did not consider the sandbox. The CI settings have no sandbox.credentials block (the key dates from Claude Code 2.1.187; the runs use 2.1.278). Since 0.3.0 the gate's build, test and lint do not run in the session, and since 0.3.2 no project target does (the evidence writer leaves a deferred mark, the in-session preflight defers to the runner's own, and the verifier reads the previous gate record and the logs): the runner runs them after the session, outside the sandbox (so without its network allow-list), with the model credentials and the workflow token removed from their environment; the build preflight's test target runs on the runner before the session, also outside the sandbox but with the runner's whole environment, a model credential and the workflow token included.
